title: $R_{\rm e}$, or not $R_{\rm e}$: Developing $R_5\equiv R_{-2}$ as a scale radius for galaxy sizes, masses, and mass-to-light ratios
comment: 20 pages, 3 figures, 5 tables. Submitted to MNRAS. Companion Python package R5Tools available at https://github.com/A-Graham/R5Tools
summary: The effective half-light radius $R_{\rm e}$ marks an arbitrary 50-per-cent light boundary, and scaling relations involving such effective radii and their associated surface brightnesses, $μ_{\rm e}$, depend systematically on the adopted percentage. Here, a gradient-defined scale, $R_5\equiv R_{-2}$, is developed as an alternative. It is the projected radius where the logarithmic slope of the intensity profile is equal to $-2$, corresponding to a slope of the surface-brightness profile of $5.00\,\text{mag dex}^{-1}$, and the radius at which the luminosity contributed per logarithmic radial interval is maximal. It can be measured non-parametrically or with a parametrized fit. For the Sérsic $R^{1/n}$ family, the exact relation $R_5=(2n/b_n)^n\,R_{\rm e}$ is derived, with $R_5/R_{\rm e}\rightarrow{\rm e}^{1/6}\approx1.181$ as $n\rightarrow\infty$. Reparameterizing the (now $b_n$-free) $R^{1/n}$ model in terms of the observable pair $(R_5,μ_5)$ removes the non-linear (radial scale)-(concentration, $n$) coupling and because the local slope is $5\,\text{mag dex}^{-1}$ at $R_5$, correlated measurement errors in $R_5$ and $μ_5$ largely cancel when deriving the inferred total magnitude. Additionally, an exact single-integral identity is provided to relate any projected light fraction to the fraction within a sphere of the same radius. The directly observable $R_5$ is connected, through a weakly $n$-dependent factor, to the anisotropy-insensitive intrinsic radius $r_{-3}$, yielding a refined $n$-dependent Wolf-type mass estimator $M_{-3}$ and spatial mass-to-light ratio $(M_{\rm dyn}/L)_{-3}$. Past half-light substitutions in dynamical mass estimators have introduced systematic concentration-dependent offsets of 12-18 per~cent in enclosed mass and a range $>20$ per~cent in the mass-to-light ratio. Dynamical mass estimators for (dark matter)-free stellar systems are also provided.

AI.tldr: The paper replaces the arbitrary 50-percent light boundary (Re) with a gradient-defined scale R5 (where the logarithmic intensity slope equals -2) for galaxy profile analysis, deriving exact conversions for Sérsic models, improved mass estimators with reduced systematic offsets, and a deprojection identity.
AI.motivation: Effective radii and associated surface brightnesses depend arbitrarily on the chosen light fraction (50%), causing systematic biases in scaling relations and dynamical mass estimates that vary with profile concentration.
AI.method: Develops R5, the radius where the logarithmic intensity slope equals -2 (5 mag dex^-1 surface-brightness slope), as a maximally-likely observable scale. Derives analytic relations for the Sérsic family, reparameterizes the model in observable (R5, μ5) terms to remove n-R coupling, provides an exact deprojection integral identity, and constructs improved Wolf-type mass estimators.
AI.result: Derives exact R5 = (2n/bn)^n Re with limit ratio e^(1/6)≈1.181 for large n; shows measurement error cancellation in (R5, μ5); documents 12-18% systematic enclosed-mass offsets and >20% M/L offsets from past half-light-based estimators; provides concentration-dependent corrected mass estimator and dark-matter-free dynamical estimators.
AI.conclusion: The gradient-defined R5 scale provides a physically motivated, non-arbitrary alternative to effective radius that reduces systematic biases in scaling relations and dynamical mass estimates, and represents a superior framework for galaxy structural analysis.

title: Impact of Upstream Clumpiness on Supernova Remnant Forward Shock Evolution in Molecular Cloud Environments
comment: 9 pages, 12 figures
summary: Supernova remnants (SNRs) are widely considered to be the primary accelerators of Galactic cosmic rays. In recent years, detailed observations have significantly progressed for young SNRs interacting with molecular clouds, a prime example being RX J1713.7-3946. When molecular clouds are clumpy, their impact can affect not only radiation properties but also shock wave propagation. Therefore, a quantitative understanding linking observational quantities with the ambient medium structure is highly required. In this study, we perform three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations to model a molecular cloud with an inhomogeneous density structure driven by supersonic turbulence and subsequent SNR formation. To investigate various pre-supernova environments, we systematically vary the medium clumpiness by replacing gas below a threshold number density with a low-density hot gas, quantifying the relationship between the forward shock velocity and the volume filling factor of the high-density clumps. As a result, we find that at an elapsed time of 1000 yr-a typical age for a young SNR-the forward shock can evolve consistently with the fast shock velocity measured in RX J1713.7-3946, provided that the clump volume filling factor is approximately 10% or less. Considering that hadronic gamma-ray emission originates exclusively from the clumpy, high-density gas, our findings suggest that the total energy of cosmic-ray protons in RX J1713.7-3946 is higher than previously estimated, amounting to at least several percent of the typical supernova explosion energy.

AI.tldr: Three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations of supernova remnants interacting with clumpy molecular clouds show that a clump volume filling factor of ~10% or less reproduces the fast forward shock velocity observed in RX J1713.7-3946, implying higher cosmic-ray proton energy than previously estimated.

AI.conclusion: The clumpy ambient medium structure strongly controls SNR shock propagation, and accounting for it revises upward the cosmic-ray proton energy budget in RX J1713.7-3946, suggesting the hadronic gamma-ray emission originates from the high-density clumps.

title: eROSITA cosmology with galaxy groups: hot gas budget out to the virial radius
comment: Accepted for publication in A&A
summary: Non-gravitational processes that expel hot gas beyond the virial regions of groups and clusters of galaxies, known collectively as baryonic feedback, play a key role in reshaping the matter distribution of the Universe on Mpc scales. We use eROSITA observations of a complete sample of 25 galaxy groups selected from the first public release of the eROSITA-DE data (eRASS1) and identified with the Two Micron Redshift Survey optical group catalogue (2MRS). We extract and fit surface brightness (SBx) profiles and present hot gas mass and hot gas fraction profiles out to $R_{200}$. We perform a Bayesian analysis of $M_{\mathrm{gas}}-M_{\mathrm{tot}}$, $L_{\mathrm{X}}-M_{\mathrm{tot}}$, and $L_{\mathrm{X}}-M_{\mathrm{gas}}$ relations, taking into account the aperture covariance effects. At $R_{500}$, we report uniformly flat SBx profiles with a mean $β$ parameter of $0.38 \pm0.04$, steepening to $β= 0.76\pm0.19$ beyond $R_{500}$. We measure a sub-cosmic hot gas fraction at the median mass of our sample $M_{500} = 2.54\times10^{13}M_{\odot}$ of $ f_{\mathrm{gas,500}} = 4.32\pm0.42\%$. Similarly, at $R_{200}$ and the median mass $M_{\mathrm{ 200}} = 3.69\times10^{13}M_{\odot}$, we obtain $f_{\mathrm{gas,200}}=5.78\pm0.69\%$. Our $f_{\mathrm{gas}}-M_{\mathrm{tot}}$ and $L_{\mathrm{X}}-M_{\mathrm{tot}}$ relations show significant deviations from the predictions of the strong feedback variants of the FLAMINGO simulation ($2.5σ$ to $8.0σ$ tension), while fiducial FLAMINGO and BAHAMAS provide the closest match to our measurements. Using our measured baryon fractions and the \texttt{SP(k)} model, we infer a $10\%-15\%$ reduction in the matter power spectrum at $k = 5\ h\ \mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ relative to a dark matter-only universe, in agreement with fiducial FLAMINGO and BAHAMAS, while revealing a growing tension on smaller scales with the strong feedback variants.

They find flat surface brightness profiles at R500 (β=0.38±0.04), sub-cosmic hot gas fractions (f_gas,500=4.32±0.42%), and their relations favor fiducial FLAMINGO and BAHAMAS simulations over strong feedback variants, implying a 10-15% suppression of the matter power spectrum at k=5 h Mpc⁻¹.
AI.motivation: Baryonic feedback processes expel hot gas beyond galaxy group virial regions and reshape the matter distribution on Mpc scales, yet their exact impact remains poorly constrained. Understanding these processes is crucial for accurate cosmological interpretation of large-scale structure.
AI.method: The authors use eROSITA observations of a complete sample of 25 galaxy groups selected from eRASS1 and identified with the 2MRS optical catalogue. They extract and fit surface brightness profiles to derive hot gas mass and fraction profiles out to R200, and perform Bayesian fits of M_gas-M_tot, L_X-M_tot, and L_X-M_gas scaling relations, accounting for aperture covariance. Results are compared to FLAMINGO and BAHAMAS simulations, and the SP(k) model is used to infer impact on the matter power spectrum.

At the median mass M500=2.54×10¹³ M⊙, the hot gas fraction is 4.32±0.42%, and at R200 it is 5.78±0.69%. The baryon fraction measurements imply a 10-15% reduction in the matter power spectrum at k=5 h Mpc⁻¹.

title: Modelling mountains on accreting magnetized neutron stars
summary: Continuous gravitational waves from accreting neutron stars in Low Mass X-ray Binaries are one of the main targets for current and next generation ground based detectors. In order to select the most promising astrophysical sources, however, reliable predictions for the signals are required, and it is therefore necessary to develop models that consistently account for the combined effects of magnetic stresses, accretion-induced heating, and the elastic response of the crust.}{We present a model for computing the quadrupolar deformation, incorporating for the first time the coupled effects of a poloidal magnetic field, deep crustal heating, and crustal elasticity. Perturbations to the star's structure driven by the Lorentz force density and by thermally-induced density variations are computed by solving a system of linearised deformation equations in the crust, for which we consider the full elastic response, while the ocean and core treated as barotropic fluids. We identify a threshold accretion rate whose value depends on crustal microphysics and the superfluid gaps in the core, above which magnetic stresses and asymmetric accretion drive deformations of opposite sign, while below this threshold their roles are reversed. The predicted eccentricities reach magnitudes up to $\varepsilon\sim 10^{-11}$, corresponding to characteristic gravitational-wave strains accessible to next-generation detectors such as the Einstein Telescope or Cosmic Explorer, but generally below the sensitivity of current LIGO, Virgo and KAGRA interferometers. These results are consistent with the non-detection of continuous gravitational waves from accreting neutron stars in Low Mass X-ray Binaries in recent observational campaigns, but highlight the need of reliable models to understand the impact of gravitational wave emission in these systems and select relevant targets for future searches.

The model predicts eccentricities up to ~10^-11, corresponding to gravitational-wave strains detectable by next-generation detectors (Einstein Telescope, Cosmic Explorer) but generally below current LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA sensitivity, consistent with recent non-detections.
AI.motivation: Continuous gravitational waves from accreting neutron stars in LMXBs are key targets for current and next-generation detectors, but reliable signal predictions require models that consistently account for combined effects of magnetic stresses, accretion-induced heating, and crustal elasticity—which previous models did not fully couple.
AI.method: The authors compute quadrupolar deformations by solving linearised deformation equations in the crust (with full elastic response), driven by Lorentz force density and thermally-induced density variations. The ocean and core are treated as barotropic fluids. A threshold accretion rate is identified, depending on crustal microphysics and superfluid gaps in the core, which determines the sign of the deformation driven by magnetic stresses versus asymmetric accretion.
AI.result: The model predicts eccentricities up to ε~10^-11 with characteristic gravitational-wave strains accessible to next-generation detectors such as Einstein Telescope and Cosmic Explorer, but generally below the sensitivity of current LIGO, Virgo, and KAGRA interferometers.
AI.conclusion: The results are consistent with the non-detection of continuous gravitational waves from LMXB accreting neutron stars in recent campaigns, but emphasize the need for reliable models to understand gravitational-wave emission impacts in these systems and to select targets for future searches.

title: The Stellar Population of NGC 346 in the Small Magellanic Cloud with JWST
comment: Paper accepted to The Astrophysical Journal Supplement Series, 34 pages, 13 figures
summary: NGC 346 is a massive star-forming region located at a distance of $\sim$62 kpc, in the Small Magellanic Cloud (SMC). Due to its low metallicity (Z $\sim$1/5 Z$_{\odot}$), it is an ideal environment to study star formation and stellar population analogues to those at Cosmic Noon. In this work, we produce a combined JWST NIRCam and MIRI photometric catalogue of NGC 346. We characterise different stellar populations in the region: the upper main sequence (UMS), red giant branch (RGB), and red clump (RC), as well as pre-main sequence (pre-MS) stars and young stellar objects (YSOs). We performed point-spread function (PSF) weighted photometry in 11 wavelength bands across NIRCam and MIRI and utilised multiple colour-magnitude-diagrams to identify the various stellar populations in the field. Our final photometric catalogue of NGC 346 comprises 249,519 unique sources, including 2,024 UMS stars, 2,755 RGB stars and 742 RC stars. In addition, we identified 6,274 candidate pre-MS stars, 7,350 candidate YSOs and 23,819 IR-excess sources. Combining these three categories, we characterised 1,583 strong and 3,761 likely pre-MS/YSO candidates. By utilising the F115W-F200W vs F115W-F187N colour-colour diagram, we found 239 non-spurious sources with Pa$α$ excess, indicating accretion and star formation in NGC 346. Using JWST NIRCam and MIRI observations, we produced the deepest catalogue to date of the star formation region NGC 346 in the near- and mid-IR range (1-21$~μ$m). Our catalogue and characterisations of the young and old populations will provide the basis for detailed follow-up studies.

The authors characterize multiple stellar populations including UMS, RGB, RC, pre-MS stars, and YSOs, and identify 239 Paα-excess sources indicating active accretion and star formation.
AI.motivation: NGC 346, at low metallicity (Z ~1/5 Z☉), serves as a unique local analogue to star-forming environments at Cosmic Noon. A comprehensive JWST-based photometric catalogue across near- and mid-infrared wavelengths is needed to characterize its diverse stellar populations and study star formation processes under low-metallicity conditions.
AI.method: The authors performed PSF-weighted photometry in 11 wavelength bands spanning JWST NIRCam and MIRI, and used multiple colour-magnitude diagrams (CMDs) to classify stellar populations. A F115W-F200W vs F115W-F187N colour-colour diagram was employed to identify Paα-excess sources as accretion tracers.

Combining pre-MS/YSO categories yields 1,583 strong and 3,761 likely candidates, with 239 non-spurious Paα-excess sources found via the colour-colour diagnostic.
AI.conclusion: This work delivers the deepest near- and mid-IR catalogue to date of NGC 346 and robustly characterizes both young and old stellar populations, providing a foundational dataset for detailed follow-up studies of star formation in low-metallicity environments.

title: From Variability to SED Modeling: A Multiwavelength Study of the Neutrino Blazar TXS 0506+056
comment: Accepted for publication in The Astrophysical Journal. 20 pages, 12 figures
summary: The blazar TXS 0506+056 is the first source that was reported to be associated with high-energy extragalactic neutrino events and is one of the major targets for multi-messenger studies. We carried out multi-wavelength optical monitoring of this object on 24 nights in the period from 2018 to 2023. The overall light curves exhibit a dimming trend superposed by some small-amplitude fluctuations, and intraday variability was detected on four nights. Bluer-when-brighter behaviors were observed on both intraday and long timescales and were more pronounced on long timescales, while a weak redder-when-brighter trend was detected on one night. No significant time lags were found between variations at different optical wavelengths. We also retrieved the multi-broadband data from some monitoring programs. The data reveal complex, asynchronous flaring in different wavebands. A cross-correlation analysis shows that the high-energy emission (optical to gamma-ray) is co-spatial and leads the radio emission by a substantial time of about 800 to 900 days, suggesting that the radio emission originates from a downstream region of the jet. We performed time-dependent lepto-hadronic modeling of the spectral energy distributions for three representative epochs, the 2017 neutrino-associated flare, a post-flare phase, and a deep quiescent state, revealing an evolution in the radiative properties of the emission regions. The modeling results provide a phenomenological framework for interpreting the long-term multiwavelength behavior of TXS 0506+056 in a multi-messenger context.

AI.motivation: TXS 0506+056 is the first reported source associated with high-energy extragalactic neutrino events, making it a primary target for multi-messenger studies. Understanding its multi-wavelength variability and radiative properties is crucial for interpreting neutrino production mechanisms and jet physics in blazars.
AI.method: The study uses optical monitoring observations over 24 nights (2018-2023), intraday and long-timescale variability analysis, spectral color behavior (bluer-when-brighter) quantification, cross-correlation analysis between radio and high-energy bands, and time-dependent lepto-hadronic modeling of spectral energy distributions for three representative epochs.

title: Concerns regarding recurrent fluorescence's impact on smaller diffuse ISM aromatics
comment: To appear in publication
summary: Recent research implied that recurrent fluorescence (RF) could bolster smaller aromatics against fragmentation in the diffuse ISM, yet that hypothesis is contested by timescales for unrelenting dissociative recombination (electrons), and unceasing dissociating photons. Specifically, neutral cyanonaphthalene can sustain $13.6$ eV photoionization, and the ensuing cation's excess energy is channeled through intramolecular vibrational redistribution (IVR), with RF providing the radiative stabilization pathway ($\simeq7$ eV negligible survival limit). However, that cation endures dissociative recombination every $τ\approx0.5^{+5.6}_{-0.4}$ years, which deposits $\simeq 8.6$ eV and exceeds the limit. Moreover, that is paired with $7-13.6$ eV photodestruction each $τ\approx16^{+223}_{-14}$ years (total visual dust extinction $A_V=0-1$, and $τ\approx4^{+7}_{-2}$ years for $A_V\approx0$). Recent laboratory characterizations of RF were seminal, but the mechanism may not overturn models indicating a gap in smaller $N_C\approx7-11$ diffuse ISM aromatics, nor support those molecules as viable diffuse interstellar band carriers.

AI.tldr: This paper examines whether recurrent fluorescence (RF) can protect small aromatic molecules (specifically neutral cyanonaphthalene and its cation) from fragmentation in the diffuse interstellar medium (ISM). Despite RF providing radiative stabilization after photoionization, the authors find that dissociative recombination (every ~0.5 years, depositing ~8.6 eV) and photodestruction (every ~16 years for A_V=0-1, or ~4 years for A_V≈0) exceed the ~7 eV survival threshold, indicating RF cannot overturn models showing a gap in smaller aromatics (N_C≈7-11) in the diffuse ISM or support them as diffuse interstellar band carriers.
AI.motivation: Recent research suggested that recurrent fluorescence could bolster smaller aromatics against fragmentation in the diffuse ISM, but this hypothesis was contested. The authors aim to evaluate whether RF is a viable stabilization mechanism for cyanonaphthalene cations against competing destruction processes.
AI.method: The authors quantify competing destruction channels against RF-based radiative stabilization: (1) dissociative recombination with electrons (timescale τ≈0.5^{+5.6}_{-0.4} years, depositing ≈8.6 eV), and (2) photodestruction by 7-13.6 eV photons (τ≈16^{+223}_{-14} years at A_V=0-1, and τ≈4^{+7}_{-2} years at A_V≈0). These are compared against the ≈7 eV negligible survival limit for the cation.
AI.result: The dissociative recombination and photodestruction rates deposit energies (≈8.6 eV) that exceed the ≈7 eV survival limit established by RF stabilization. The destruction timescales are comparable to or shorter than relevant survival timescales, indicating that RF cannot effectively protect these molecules in the diffuse ISM.
AI.conclusion: Despite recent seminal laboratory characterizations of recurrent fluorescence, this mechanism cannot overturn existing models that predict a gap in smaller aromatics (N_C≈7-11) in the diffuse ISM, nor support these molecules as viable diffuse interstellar band (DIB) carriers.

title: NMMA-Astro-COLIBRI: An Automated Light-Curve Supernovae Classification Service in the Multi-Survey Era
summary:
The surge in publicly available photometric alerts from wide-field surveys requires automated tools for real-time transient classification. We present NMMA--Astro-COLIBRI, an on-demand Bayesian classification service that couples the Nuclear-physics and Multi-Messenger Astrophysics (NMMA) inference framework to the Astro-COLIBRI real-time multi-messenger platform. After the detection of an optical transient, if photometry is available, it is quality-filtered. The filtered photometry is fitted by nested sampling against a user-selected model from a library of eleven supernova templates; results are delivered to every user within minutes. Applying two or more models on the same optical transient, the service reports the corresponding log Bayes factors as a quantitative ranking of competing subtypes.
  We demonstrate the workflow on SN 2021ugl (ZTF21abotose), a Type IIb supernova initially mistaken for a kilonova candidate by automated real-time pipelines, comparing competing supernova and kilonova models. In an early-time configuration using only the first ~ 6 days of photometry in two bands (ZTF g and r), so ten days before spectroscopic confirmation, the empirical Type IIb template recovers the correct classification, favored over both the kilonova template and the kilonova-mimicking shock-cooling model. In the full 47-day, three-band baseline, it again achieves the highest evidence over every competing supernova and kilonova template. These results highlight the importance of a comprehensive supernova template library for kilonova discrimination in the multi-survey era.

AI.tldr: The paper presents NMMA-Astro-COLIBRI, an on-demand Bayesian classification service that couples the NMMA inference framework with the Astro-COLIBRI real-time multi-messenger platform. It delivers fast supernova subtype classification from photometric alerts using nested sampling against eleven supernova templates and reports log Bayes factors for model comparison. Demonstrated on SN 2021ugl, the service correctly classified a Type IIb supernova—originally flagged as a kilonova candidate—using early-time photometry, well before spectroscopic confirmation.
AI.motivation: The increasing volume of photometric alerts from wide-field surveys demands automated, real-time tools for transient classification to enable prompt follow-up and reduce misclassifications of transients such as supernovae being mistaken for kilonovae.
AI.method: The system couples the NMMA inference framework to the Astro-COLIBRI real-time platform. Detected optical transients have their photometry quality-filtered, then fitted via nested sampling against a user-selected model from eleven supernova templates. Applying multiple models yields log Bayes factors for quantitative ranking of competing subtypes.
AI.result: Demonstrated on SN 2021ugl (ZTF21abotose), a Type IIb supernova initially mistaken for a kilonova. Using only the first ~6 days of two-band photometry (10 days before spectroscopic confirmation), the empirical Type IIb template gave the correct classification over kilonova and shock-cooling models. With a full 47-day three-band baseline, it achieved the highest evidence among all competing templates.
AI.conclusion: A comprehensive supernova template library is essential for robust kilonova discrimination in the multi-survey era. The NMMA-Astro-COLIBRI service provides rapid, quantitative Bayesian classification enabling correct identification of optical transients in real time.

title: The segmented spiral structure of the Solar neighbourhood traced by young clustered populations
comment: 12 pages, 4 figures, 5 tables. Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: The Milky Way spiral pattern remains poorly constrained, and the youngest tracers in the solar neighbourhood do not always follow a few smooth, continuous logarithmic arms. We analyse young open clusters, both independently and combined with young stellar object (YSO)-based groups, to test whether they define continuous spiral-arm ridges or shorter, partially connected structures. In the (theta_G, ln R_G) plane, we identify local overdensities using a density-supported Bayesian Gaussian Mixture Model (BGMM), introducing published Perseus, Local, Sagittarius, and Scutum arm tracks only afterwards as reference curves. We then apply a Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) analysis in the heliocentric (X,Y) plane to examine spatial connectivity. The open-cluster sample already resolves into several local components, while the addition of YSO-based groups highlights branches and intermediate regions without producing continuous arms. The MST likewise shows distinct local branches at small pruning scales that progressively merge as the linking scale increases. The Local--Sagittarius region provides the clearest agreement between both diagnostics: the BGMM identifies an intermediate component between the reference arms, while the MST connects neighbouring branches through the same region. Overall, young structures near the Sun appear as fragmented, spiral-like segments with partial links rather than smooth continuations of a few grand-design arms. Determining whether this morphology reflects spiral-arm formation mechanisms or subsequent evolution will require additional age, vertical, and kinematic information.

AI.tldr: This paper tests whether young open clusters and YSO-based groups in the solar neighbourhood form continuous spiral-arm ridges or fragmented, partially connected structures. Using a Bayesian Gaussian Mixture Model (BGMM) for density-based clustering in the (θ_G, ln R_G) plane and a Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) analysis in the heliocentric (X,Y) plane, the authors find that young tracers resolve into multiple local components and branches rather than smooth continuations of grand-design spiral arms. The Local–Sagittarius region shows the best agreement between the two diagnostics, revealing an intermediate component partially linking neighbouring branches.
AI.motivation: The Milky Way spiral pattern is poorly constrained, and the youngest tracers near the Sun do not consistently follow a few smooth, continuous logarithmic arms. The authors aim to determine whether young open clusters and YSO-based groups define continuous spiral-arm ridges or shorter, partially connected structures, which has implications for understanding spiral-arm formation and evolution.
AI.method: The analysis uses a density-supported Bayesian Gaussian Mixture Model (BGMM) to identify local overdensities in the (θ_G, ln R_G) plane, with published Perseus, Local, Sagittarius, and Scutum arm tracks introduced only afterwards as reference curves. A Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) analysis is then applied in the heliocentric (X,Y) plane to examine spatial connectivity at various pruning scales. Young open clusters are analysed both independently and combined with YSO-based groups.
AI.result: The open-cluster sample resolves into several local components, and adding YSO-based groups highlights branches and intermediate regions without producing continuous arms. The MST shows distinct local branches at small pruning scales that merge as the linking scale increases. The Local–Sagittarius region shows the clearest agreement: the BGMM identifies an intermediate component between reference arms, and the MST connects neighbouring branches through the same region.
AI.conclusion: Young structures near the Sun appear as fragmented, spiral-like segments with partial links rather than smooth continuations of a few grand-design arms. Determining whether this morphology reflects spiral-arm formation mechanisms or subsequent evolution will require additional age, vertical, and kinematic information.

title: SST-1M: Recent results and prospects for observation of the Galactic Center region
comment: 7 pages, 8 figures. Proceedings for the IAU Symposium 405 "Traversing the Galactic Center in Space and Time"
summary: The Galactic Center is a crowded region containing powerful particle accelerators and objects producing non-thermal radiation, including the diffuse very-high-energy (VHE) gamma-ray component known as the `Ridge', whose hard spectrum suggests particle acceleration up to PeV energies. The relevant processes can be tested, and the source parameters can be constrained via Cherenkov telescope observations. Two Single-Mirror Small-Size Cherenkov Telescopes (SST-1M) are currently operated in stereoscopic mode at the Ondřejov Observatory. Their future relocation is being considered, including a site with excellent visibility of the Galactic Center. We present recent observations demonstrating SST-1M capabilities for detecting extended emission and discuss prospects for probing the Galactic Center region, including searches for a spectral cut-off above 10 TeV. We show that the large field-of-view and good VHE sensitivity make SST-1M an ideal instrument for the search for PeVatrons.

AI.tldr: The paper discusses the capabilities of the SST-1M Cherenkov telescopes for observing the Galactic Center's diffuse VHE gamma-ray emission (the "Ridge"), which may trace PeV-scale particle acceleration. It presents recent observations demonstrating the telescopes' ability to detect extended emission and explores their potential for probing the region, including searching for a spectral cut-off above 10 TeV.
AI.motivation: The Galactic Center contains powerful particle accelerators producing non-thermal radiation, including the diffuse VHE gamma-ray "Ridge" whose hard spectrum hints at PeV-scale particle acceleration (PeVatrons). Testing the relevant acceleration processes and constraining source parameters requires dedicated Cherenkov telescope observations.
AI.method: The study uses two Single-Mirror Small-Size Cherenkov Telescopes (SST-1M) operated in stereoscopic mode at the Ondřejov Observatory. It presents recent observations demonstrating the telescopes' capabilities for detecting extended emission, and evaluates their prospects for observing the Galactic Center, including searches for spectral cut-offs above 10 TeV. A future relocation to a site with excellent Galactic Center visibility is considered.
AI.result: The large field-of-view and good VHE sensitivity of SST-1M make it well-suited for detecting extended emission and probing the Galactic Center region, positioning it as an ideal instrument for the search for PeVatrons.
AI.conclusion: SST-1M is a capable instrument for studying the Galactic Center's VHE gamma-ray emission and searching for spectral cut-offs above 10 TeV, making it well-suited for PeVatron searches, particularly if relocated to a site with better Galactic Center visibility.

title: The Spin Angular Momentum and Black Hole Mass Components of Sagittarius A*
comment: 6 pages, summary of oral report presented at the Galactic Center workshop 2026 (IAU Symposium 405, Traversing the Galactic Center in Space and Time)
summary: The dimensionless spin angular momentum, dimensionless spin function, and blackhole mass components of Sagittarius A* (Sgr A*) were obtained by Daly et al. (2024) by applying the outflow method to six independent sets of simultaneously or contemporaneously obtained X-ray and radio data. Here, results obtained for Sgr A* with the outflow method are reviewed. Consistent results were obtained with each data set. Set I (the preferred data set) indicates that Sgr A* has a dimensionless spin angular momentum $a_* = (0.90 ~\pm~ 0.06)$ and a dimensionless spin function $F = (0.62 ~\pm~ 0.10)$. The results are consistent with the value of $a_* = (0.93~\pm~ 0.15)$ obtained with the outflow method applied to an independent data set (Daly 2019). The application of the outflow method to a weak compact radio source such as Sgr A* in its current state is most accurately determined with simultaneous or contemporaneous radio and X-ray measurements.

AI.tldr: This paper reviews the application of the outflow method to Sgr A* using six independent X-ray and radio data sets, finding consistent results. The preferred data set yields a dimensionless spin angular momentum a* = 0.90 ± 0.06 and spin function F = 0.62 ± 0.10, consistent with earlier independent estimates (a* = 0.93 ± 0.15). The method is most accurate with simultaneous/contemporaneous measurements for weak compact radio sources.
AI.motivation: To review and consolidate the outflow method results for Sgr A* obtained by Daly et al. (2024), assessing the consistency across multiple independent data sets and validating the derived black hole spin parameters.
AI.method: The outflow method is applied to six independent sets of simultaneously or contemporaneously obtained X-ray and radio data to derive the dimensionless spin angular momentum, dimensionless spin function, and black hole mass components of Sgr A*. Results from each data set are compared for consistency.
AI.result: Consistent results were obtained across all six data sets. The preferred data set (Set I) gives a* = 0.90 ± 0.06 and F = 0.62 ± 0.10 for Sgr A*. These results are consistent with an earlier independent application of the outflow method (Daly 2019) that yielded a* = 0.93 ± 0.15.
AI.conclusion: The outflow method provides consistent spin estimates for Sgr A* across multiple data sets. For weak compact radio sources in their current state, simultaneous or contemporaneous radio and X-ray measurements yield the most accurate results.

title: Revisiting neutrino event epochs for the blazar PKS 0735+178 with TESS
comment: Accepted for publication in ApJ, 13 pages, 6 figures, 1 table
summary: We present here the results of the optical light curve variability analysis of the blazars PKS 0735+178, in weeks-scale flare state, observed in three sectors with the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS). The TESS observations in this study coincide with a well-known neutrino emission phase detected with four different neutrino observatories at multiple epochs in a narrow time window. We segmented the rising and decaying parts of the flare and individually analyzed their flux distribution, excess variance, variability timescale, and the power spectral density (PSD). The source displayed an elevated excess variance of ~25%, with a multi-modal flux distribution (coherent in the rising and distorted in the decaying phase). The variability timescale analysis highlights a much faster decay than the rising scale, and the PSDs depict a nominal change in the power spectral slope. We discuss a likely connection in the optical variations and the neutrino events, and briefly explain a possible physical scenario for the observed optical flux behavior in view of previously discovered radio-band results.

AI.tldr: Analysis of optical light curve variability of blazar PKS 0735+178 during a weeks-scale flare observed with TESS, coinciding with neutrino emission detected by four observatories. The study segments rising/decaying flare phases to analyze flux distribution, excess variance (~25%), variability timescales (faster decay than rise), and power spectral density (nominal slope change), discussing potential optical-neutrino connection and physical scenarios.
AI.motivation: To characterize the optical variability of blazar PKS 0735+178 during a flare phase coincident with a narrow-window neutrino emission episode detected by multiple neutrino observatories, and to explore possible connections between optical flux behavior and neutrino production.
AI.method: The flare was segmented into rising and decaying phases. Each phase was independently analyzed for flux distribution, excess variance, variability timescale, and power spectral density using TESS photometric observations across three sectors.
AI.result: The source showed elevated excess variance (~25%), a multi-modal flux distribution (coherent in rising phase, distorted in decaying phase), significantly faster decay timescale than rising timescale, and a nominal change in the power spectral slope across the phases.
AI.conclusion: The optical variability features likely connect to the coincident neutrino events, and the observed asymmetric flare behavior can be physically explained within the context of previously discovered radio-band results.

title: The initial evolution of SN 2011dh: The importance of inhomogeneities
comment: 30 pages, 6 figures, 1 appendix, accepted to ApJ
summary:
SN 2011dh is rather unique in that it offered detailed observations of the initial phase in the radio as well as optical regimes. This makes possible a comparison between models used to deduce properties of the outer envelope of the supernova ejecta. It is shown that a consistent description suggests the forward shock to have started in the piston phase with constant velocity, and only later, around 50 days, transitioned to the standard model, which is independent of initial conditions. In addition, observations imply that the radio source is inhomogeneous with a covering factor of, approximately, 50%.
  It is emphasised that the deduced properties of the synchrotron source are very sensitive to the presence of inhomogeneities; for example, a covering factor of 50% increases the ratio of the energy densities of relativistic electrons and magnetic field by several orders of magnitude as compared to a homogeneous source. The shallow density gradient in the envelope causes substantial deceleration of the forward shock. This is used to argue that the magnetic field strength scales inversely with radius rather than inversely with time; this is similar to SN 1993J. Attention is also drawn to the similarities between the flat spectra of compact, extragalatic radio sources and the evolution of radio supernovae; e.g., the scaling of the magnetic field and the constant brightness temperature.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes SN 2011dh, a supernova uniquely observed in both radio and optical regimes during its initial phase. The study finds the forward shock began in a constant-velocity piston phase before transitioning to the standard model around day 50. The radio source is inhomogeneous with a ~50% covering factor, which drastically affects derived properties like the electron-to-magnetic-field energy density ratio. The shallow density gradient causes significant shock deceleration, and the magnetic field is argued to scale inversely with radius (rather than time), similar to SN 1993J. The authors also note parallels between compact extragalactic radio sources and radio supernovae.
AI.motivation: To exploit SN 2011dh's rare dual-band (radio and optical) observations of the early phase to discriminate between competing models of the supernova ejecta's outer envelope, and to highlight the role of inhomogeneities in interpreting synchrotron source properties.
AI.method: The authors compare models used to deduce outer-envelope properties from radio and optical observations of SN 2011dh. They analyze the forward shock evolution (piston vs. standard phases), infer the radio source's covering factor from inhomogeneity, examine energy density ratios of relativistic electrons and magnetic fields under homogeneous vs. inhomogeneous assumptions, and derive magnetic field scaling by relating shock deceleration to the envelope's density gradient.
AI.result: A consistent description indicates the forward shock started in a constant-velocity piston phase and transitioned to the standard model around day 50. The radio source is inhomogeneous with a covering factor of ~50%, which increases the electron-to-magnetic-field energy density ratio by several orders of magnitude versus a homogeneous source. The shallow density gradient causes substantial shock deceleration, supporting a magnetic field scaling inversely with radius (as in SN 1993J) rather than with time.
AI.conclusion: SN 2011dh's early radio and optical data reveal a two-phase shock evolution and an inhomogeneous radio source, emphasizing the strong sensitivity of deduced synchrotron source properties to inhomogeneities. The magnetic field scaling inversely with radius and the analogy with compact extragalactic radio sources (e.g., constant brightness temperature) suggest broader universal behaviors in radio-emitting sources.

title: The high entropy of the UHECR arrival direction distribution favors a light composition
summary: We analyze the constraints on the composition of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs), and on the density and distribution of their sources, that may be inferred from their arrival-direction distribution, using a novel semi-analytical description of the propagation energy loss of atomic nuclei ($A>4$) with energy $>2\times10^{19}~\text{eV}$, that allows generating UHECR arrival maps faster than by using detailed propagation simulations and yields insights to the impact of propagation energy loss. We show that the anisotropy of the UHECR arrival direction distribution due to the large-scale structure (LSS) of matter distribution is larger for heavy nuclei composition compared to protons, despite their larger deflections by magnetic fields, due to their shorter propagation distance and weaker dependence of rigidity on observed energy. Identifying the LSS anisotropy signal is hampered for heavy nuclei due to their large deflections by the uncertain Galactic magnetic field (GMF). We introduce a new measure of anisotropy, an "entropy" of the arrival-direction distribution, that is largely independent of the GMF configuration and has strong discriminating power between heavy- and light-composition models. Analyzing the public $>3.2\times10^{19}$~eV Auger data, we show that the correlation with the LSS on large angular scales is weak and requires a low source density, $s_0\le10^{-4}{\rm Mpc}^{-3}$, to allow masking the LSS signature by "cosmic-variance" ($s_0=10^{-2}{\rm Mpc}^{-3}$ is ruled out at $>99\%$ confidence level (CL)). The high entropy of the distribution is consistent with proton models and inconsistent with heavy nuclei models at $>96\%$ CL for $s_0\ge10^{-5}{\rm Mpc}^{-3}$. Reducing the absolute energy calibration uncertainty may allow detection of the LSS correlation for proton models (increased exposure alone will not suffice due to the dominance of cosmic variance).

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a semi-analytical framework for rapidly simulating UHECR arrival directions and shows that the LSS-induced anisotropy is larger for heavy nuclei than protons despite stronger magnetic deflections. A new GMF-independent "entropy" measure of anisotropy is proposed. Analysis of Auger data finds weak LSS correlation (requiring low source density s0≤1e-4 Mpc^-3) and an entropy consistent with proton composition while ruling out heavy nuclei at >96% CL for s0≥1e-5 Mpc^-3.
AI.motivation: To understand the composition and source distribution of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays from their arrival-direction anisotropy, while overcoming the computational burden of detailed propagation simulations and the confounding effect of the Galactic magnetic field.
AI.method: A novel semi-analytical description of the propagation energy loss of heavy nuclei (A>4) at E>2e19 eV enables fast generation of arrival maps. A new "entropy" anisotropy measure, largely independent of the GMF configuration, is introduced. The framework is applied to public Auger data above 3.2e19 eV to constrain source density and composition.
AI.result: LSS anisotropy is larger for heavy nuclei than protons due to shorter propagation distances and weaker rigidity dependence. Heavy nuclei deflections by the GMF hamper LSS detection. Auger data show weak LSS correlation, requiring s0≤1e-4 Mpc^-3 (s0=1e-2 Mpc^-3 excluded >99% CL). The measured high entropy is consistent with protons and inconsistent with heavy nuclei at >96% CL for s0≥1e-5 Mpc^-3. Energy calibration improvements, not just increased exposure, are needed to detect LSS correlation in proton models.
AI.conclusion: The composition of UHECRs above ~3e19 eV is likely proton-dominated rather than heavy-nucleus-dominated, and source densities are low (≤1e-4 Mpc^-3). Reduced energy calibration uncertainty is essential for future LSS detection, as increased exposure alone will not overcome cosmic variance.

title: Evidence of self-organized criticality in the prompt emission of a bright gamma-ray burst
comment: 22 pages, 12 figures, accepted for publication in ApJL
summary: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) are the most energetic explosive events in the Universe, yet the physical mechanism of their prompt emission remains a mystery. Especially, it is unclear whether the energy dissipation mechanism in the GRB jet is dominated by kinetic energy or magnetic energy. Here, we studied the pulses in the prompt emission of the second brightest GRB to date, GRB 230307A, which was accurately measured by the Gravitational wave high-energy electromagnetic counterpart all-sky monitor (GECAM), with focus on the cumulative distributions of peak counts and duration of pulses as well as the waiting time between pulses. We find that these cumulative distributions show scale-invariant behavior, well consistent with the prediction of the self-organized criticality (SOC) theory. This is the first robust evidence of an SOC feature in the prompt emission of a single GRB. Moreover, the statistical properties of pulses in the prompt emission of GRB 230307A are very similar to those of solar flares. Our findings suggest that the prompt emission of GRB is powered by the dissipation of magnetic energy in the ultra-relativistic jet, supporting the Poynting-flux-dominated prompt models.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the prompt emission pulses of GRB 230307A (the second brightest GRB) using GECAM data, finding that the cumulative distributions of peak counts, pulse durations, and waiting times exhibit scale-invariant behavior consistent with self-organized criticality (SOC) theory. This provides the first robust SOC evidence in a single GRB's prompt emission, with statistical properties similar to solar flares, suggesting the prompt emission is powered by magnetic energy dissipation in a Poynting-flux-dominated jet.
AI.motivation: The physical mechanism of GRB prompt emission is unresolved, particularly whether the energy dissipation in the GRB jet is dominated by kinetic or magnetic energy. This study aims to constrain the dissipation mechanism by examining the statistical properties of pulses in individual GRBs.
AI.method: The authors studied pulses in the prompt emission of GRB 230307A using high-precision data from GECAM. They analyzed the cumulative distributions of three quantities: peak counts, pulse durations, and waiting times between pulses, and compared these distributions against predictions from self-organized criticality (SOC) theory.
AI.result: The cumulative distributions of peak counts, durations, and waiting times all show scale-invariant behavior consistent with SOC theory predictions. This constitutes the first robust evidence of SOC features in the prompt emission of a single GRB. Additionally, the pulse statistical properties of GRB 230307A closely resemble those of solar flares.
AI.conclusion: The findings suggest that GRB prompt emission is powered by magnetic energy dissipation in the ultra-relativistic jet, supporting Poynting-flux-dominated prompt emission models.

title: Generalized Non-linear Bayesian Pulsar Timing with Enterprise
comment: 34 pages, 15 figures, 2 appendices, accepted by The Astrophysical Journal
summary: In this study, we use the Bayesian methods in the Enterprise package to examine the fully general parameterization of pulsar timing models in tandem with noise. We investigate four pulsars, PSR J1600$-$3053, PSR J2043+1711, PSR J0740+6620, and PSR J1640+2224, through the lens of Bayesian timing. These four are selected as they are well-studied, but exhibit interesting characteristics under the lens of Bayesian timing. Our new pulsar mass constraints (medians and 68\% confidence intervals) for our fully general non-linear Bayesian timing models are $m_{\mathrm{p}}=1.6(1)~\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ for PSR J2043+1711 and $m_{\mathrm{p}}=2.3^{+0.9}_{-0.7}~\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ for PSR J1600$-$3053 both using the NANOGrav 12.5-yr data release, and $m_{\mathrm{p}}=2.06(6)~\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ for PSR J0740+6620 using the data from Fonseca, et al., 2021. We investigate the effects on placing physical priors on timing model parameters, including restricting the upper limit on the pulsar mass for PSR J1640+2224, which has a mass often estimated to be greater than $3~\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$. We find \ark{that restricting the allowed sampling space of the pulsar mass for PSR J1640+2224 to} $m_{\mathrm{p}}<3~\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ results in a pulsar mass of $m_{\mathrm{p}}=2.2(5)~\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$ for PSR J1640+2224 using the NANOGrav 12.5-yr data release. For the first time, we find evidence for intrinsic red noise in PSR J2043+1711. We show how fully general Bayesian timing can better model the interplay of the intrinsic noise and the timing parameters.

AI.tldr: The paper applies fully general Bayesian pulsar timing models using the Enterprise package to four well-studied pulsars, yielding new mass constraints (e.g., 1.6(1) M☉ for J2043+1711, 2.3+0.9/−0.7 M☉ for J1600−3053, 2.06(6) M☉ for J0740+6620), demonstrates the effect of physical priors including restricting J1640+2224's mass below 3 M☉ (resulting in 2.2(5) M☉), and reports first evidence for intrinsic red noise in J2043+1711.
AI.motivation: To examine the fully general parameterization of pulsar timing models in tandem with noise using Bayesian methods, addressing how prior choices and noise modeling affect pulsar mass constraints and the interplay between noise and timing parameters.
AI.method: Bayesian timing analysis using the Enterprise package on four pulsars (J1600−3053, J2043+1711, J0740+6620, J1640+2224), using NANOGrav 12.5-yr data and data from Fonseca et al. 2021, with fully general non-linear Bayesian timing models, including tests of physical priors on timing model parameters.
AI.result: New pulsar mass constraints: mp=1.6(1) M☉ for J2043+1711 and mp=2.3+0.9/−0.7 M☉ for J1600−3053 (NANOGrav 12.5-yr); mp=2.06(6) M☉ for J0740+6620 (Fonseca et al. 2021 data). Restricting J1640+2224's mass below 3 M☉ yields mp=2.2(5) M☉. First evidence for intrinsic red noise in J2043+1711 is reported.
AI.conclusion: Fully general Bayesian timing can better model the interplay of intrinsic noise and timing parameters, and physical priors significantly affect derived pulsar properties such as mass.
